    Add the domains to a Seurat or SpatialExperiment object

    Source: R/inputs.R
    add_domains.Rd

    add_domains() writes the result of sigdots() into the per-spot metadata of the object the data came from, so that the domains can be used like any other per-spot label (plotting, subsetting, differential expression). Two columns are added: sigdots_domain, the domain number of every spot (NA for a spot in a part of the tree that could not be tested), and sigdots_candidate_domain, the candidate domain the spot was in.

    Usage

    add_domains(object, fit, prefix = "sigdots")

    Arguments

    object

    A Seurat object, or a SpatialExperiment, SingleCellExperiment or SummarizedExperiment object. Its cells or spots must be exactly those fit was computed on, in the same order (which is the case when fit came from sigdots(object, ...)).

    fit

    A result of sigdots().

    prefix

    The first part of the two column names ("sigdots" by default, giving sigdots_domain and sigdots_candidate_domain). Use another prefix to keep the results of several runs side by side.

    Value

    The object with the two columns added: in object[[]] (the metadata) for a Seurat object, in colData(object) for the others.

    Details

    The spots are matched by their identifiers (the column names of the object and the spot identifiers of fit), so the object may hold its spots in a different order, but it must not hold spots that fit does not have; such spots stop the function with an error naming the first of them. Existing columns with the same names are replaced.

    See also

    domains() for the same information as a plain table.

    Examples

    # \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("SpatialExperiment", quietly = TRUE)) {
  spe <- SpatialExperiment::SpatialExperiment(
    assays = list(logcounts = t(sigdots_example$x)), spatialCoords = sigdots_example$coords)
  fit <- sigdots(spe, K0 = 5, verbose = FALSE)
  spe <- add_domains(spe, fit)
  table(SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe)$sigdots_domain)
}
#> 
#>   1   2   3 
#> 300 300 300 
# }
